claims.claim: The Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9) governs how mixed-direction runs, isolates and neutral characters such as percent and currency signs resolve, which is why a bare integer is safe inside an RTL run but a digit adjacent to a symbol needs isolation.
WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.3 requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text (3:1 for large text), which is the threshold the HyperFrames contrast pass enforces.

Setting dir="rtl" or dir="auto" on the <html> element previews and snapshots correctly but renders a fully blank/black MP4. Upstream ships this as lint rule html_dir_attribute_breaks_render at severity error.
claims.raw_snippet: renders correctly in preview/snapshot but produces a fully blank/black video from render

claims.claim: Upstream lints `repeat: Math.ceil(...) - 1` as gsap_repeat_ceil_overshoot and prescribes `repeat: Math.max(0, Math.floor(totalDuration / cycleDuration) - 1)` instead, because ceil runs one cycle past the composition duration.

`class="clip"` is a convention the runtime never reads, but the scaffold's shared `.clip { position: absolute; inset: 0 }` rule supplies the full-frame scene box and lint warns via timed_element_missing_clip_class when a visible timed element lacks it.
claims.raw_snippet: `class="clip"` is a **convention, not a requirement**: the runtime never reads it.

claims.claim: Both bundled scripts default their capture viewport to 1920x1080 and 30fps, so a 1080x1920 portrait composition must be given --width/--height or every bounding box, flag and contrast sample is computed against the wrong frame.
